sus.reason: I would use the website if it produced a proper book about Lily and Conker, but not in its present form.
The forms were fairly straightforward, but the technical wording, hidden fields and confusing errors made the whole job more complicated than necessary.
I could manage the form with clear labels and large buttons, but the tiny page controls and weak grey text made it tiring at 200% zoom.
I managed the basic steps without help, but I would want someone to show me how to fix the story, pictures and payment problems.
The steps generally followed in order, but the choices did not carry through properly to the finished book.
The selected style, title, story, pictures and checkout details did not agree with one another.
A person with steady eyesight might get on quickly, but small controls, pale text and unexplained choices would stop many older people.
It was not dreadful to fill in, but I had to work hard to read the small controls and check the finished pages.
I felt fairly confident filling in the form, but not confident about the book, the unexpected gift wrap or the final cost.
I did not need a long lesson, but I did need to learn what several technical words meant.

interview.purpose: This is for making a personalised storybook featuring a child and the people and memories that matter to them. It is especially for parents or relatives who want to keep a story for a child.
interview.worst_moment: The finished book was the worst moment. The title was misspelt, the pictures were in the wrong style, Conker was missing and the story ended in the middle of a sentence. I could not give that to Lily as a proper keepsake.
interview.best_moment: The best moment was entering the memory in my own words and choosing the classic storybook pictures. The steps felt reassuringly simple once the questions were clear.
interview.abandon: I would probably have given up when the book came out with the wrong title, wrong style, missing Conker and an unfinished ending. At 200% zoom, the tiny page arrows would also have made me stop if I could not read or hit them.
interview.missing: I expected a simple story about me carving Conker, giving it to Lily at Christmas and riding it with her across the Norfolk fields. I also expected to edit the story, see every page comfortably, and check that the pictures and words matched before paying.
interview.trust: I would be careful about entering family information until I knew the site would keep it safe and use it properly. I was particularly wary of the preselected £7.99 gift wrap and the countdown pressuring me at checkout.
interview.willingness_to_pay: I would pay about £10 for a proper digital storybook if it were correct, and perhaps £15 to £20 for a nicely printed copy. I would pay more only after seeing the corrected title, complete story, correct pictures and clear total price with no surprise extras.
interview.output_verdict: I was disappointed and frustrated. It was not the loving book I wanted for Lily, and I would not trust it as a keepsake without a great deal of checking and correcting.

recommendations.change: Rewrite the story as a short, simple memory about Harold carving Conker, giving it to Lily at Christmas and taking her on an imaginary gallop across the Norfolk fields.
recommendations.why: The story must sound like my family memory and be suitable for a four-year-old, not a frightening generic adventure full of grandadventure words.

recommendations.change: Correct “Adventrue”, “Lil”, “all way home” and every other visible spelling or template error, complete the final sentence and remove repeated text and the duplicated “The End”.
recommendations.why: A keepsake with obvious mistakes would be embarrassing to hand to Lily and would make me doubt the whole book.

recommendations.change: Redraw Lily with her strawberry-blonde bob and pink wellies, and show Harold and Conker consistently in the relevant pictures.
recommendations.why: The people and the hand-carved horse are the heart of the story. Conker being absent from the pictures makes the book miss its purpose.

recommendations.change: Use the requested classic ink-and-colour storybook style instead of changing it to Pop-art comic, and check that each picture matches the words on its page.
recommendations.page: Choose the look & feel / Generated storybook preview
recommendations.why: I selected a particular style, and I need to know the finished book looks like the one I ordered.

recommendations.change: Replace tiny icon-only page arrows and other small controls with large, clearly labelled buttons such as “Previous page” and “Next page”.
recommendations.why: At 200% zoom the arrows were hard to see and difficult to hit. I should be able to inspect all nine pages independently.

recommendations.change: Make all text and important instructions high contrast, especially the home page explanation, form examples and footer links.
recommendations.page: Home page / Create your book / all pages
recommendations.why: Pale grey writing is effectively invisible to me and turns ordinary reading into a struggle.

recommendations.change: Remove the countdown and do not preselect paid gift wrap or any other extra that I did not request.
recommendations.why: A countdown makes a straightforward purchase feel hurried, and the unexpected £7.99 made me suspicious of the total.

recommendations.change: Explain the reading-level choices in plain English and state why a level was selected for a four-year-old.
recommendations.why: “Lexile 200L–500L” is workshop jargon to me, and I should understand an important choice before I make it.

recommendations.change: Explain the dashboard error and profile-sync problem, with a clear way to recover without making me think I have done something wrong.
recommendations.why: The unexplained error worried me and made the account seem unreliable.

recommendations.change: Keep important fields and the Next button visible where possible, with proper visible labels for login fields and the photo upload.
recommendations.page: Log in / Create your book / Optional photo upload
recommendations.why: I should not have to hunt for the next action or guess what an empty box means, especially at high zoom.

one_line_verdict: The site took my details and made a book, but the result was more like a rough plank with the nails showing than a keepsake I would be proud to give Lily.
